title: Gratitude and meaningful coincidence
header_line: My analysis of one book on habits. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What would shift if you started each day by saying what you are grateful for?
A student tied it to the second law, make it attractive: if you keep going back to I am grateful for this opportunity, you focus on the positive when the negative things come up, which is just life.

The student gave a perspective example: late to a meeting because of a delay on the road, but seeing that someone else is having a far worse day, so that being late is not so bad. This is the student's account, with the details left out.
The student said that every morning with your coffee you could say ten things you are grateful for, and at first you think about it but then it becomes automatic.
I said that we have the ability to choose our bundle, and to say: that is a fabricated reality that I do not accept, I am creating my own reality. I have a choice.
I said that gratitude, values and priorities, stated openly, set you up for awareness in yourself and in others.

I described synchronicity as the coincidental occurrence of an event that has meaning, such as meeting someone and feeling a connection. I said that when you are grateful and clear about your intention, you meet people who share it, and meaningful coincidences follow. I said I do not mean it in a religious or hippie way.
What are you grateful for today, and what would you notice if you looked for it?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write ten things you are grateful for.
Write what you will anchor it to each morning.
Write a time a coincidence helped you.
Write who you are meeting that shares your intention.
Write what you choose not to accept from the fabricated world.

check.q: What did a student say to say each morning with coffee?
choices: Ten things you are grateful for

check.q: What did I say we have the ability to choose?
What did I say synchronicity is?

recap: Start the day with gratitude. Choose your reality. Look for coincidences.
